statement: A variance upper bound C n/log n does not, by itself, imply a fluctuation power exponent chi<1/2. There exist nonnegative random variables X_n with Var(X_n)=n/log n and lim log(sd(X_n))/log n=1/2.
assumptions: Integer n>=2; chi defined as lim log(sd(X_n))/log n when the limit exists.
source: owner-own-work; elementary counterexample, not an FPP law
proof: Take B_n with Bernoulli(1/2) marginal and X_n=2 sqrt(n/log n) B_n. Then Var(X_n)=n/log n, and log(sd(X_n))/log n=1/2-(log log n)/(2 log n), which tends to 1/2.
independent_reviewer: w365 (requested in forthcoming packet; not yet reviewed)
remaining_gap: This distinguishes logarithmic subdiffusivity from strict power subdiffusivity; it says nothing about the variance of an actual iid FPP model.
novelty: Restates the recorded campaign obstruction at-p0104; elementary, no novelty claim

statement: For weights in [a,b], 0<a<=b<infinity, T(0,n e1) is attained by a simple path contained in the deterministic l1 ball of radius floor(bn/a), and equals the finite-graph minimum there.
assumptions: Nearest-neighbor Z^d, integer n>=1; all weights bounded in [a,b]; independence is unnecessary for this deterministic statement.
source: owner-own-work reconstruction; ADH arXiv:1511.03262v2 Lemma 3.3 gives the bounded-weight path-length argument
proof: The straight path costs at most bn. A competing path of cost <=bn uses <=floor(bn/a) edges and stays in that ball. Deleting cycles strictly lowers cost. There are finitely many simple candidates; their attained minimum beats every path of cost >bn. ATTEMPT.md L1.
remaining_gap: Does not cover zero or unbounded weights.

statement: For any finite iid Bernoulli(p) product and real f, with delta_i=f(eta_-i,1)-f(eta_-i,0), independent-coordinate retention/resampling eta^rho, and R(rho)=p(1-p) sum_i E[delta_i f(eta)delta_i f(eta^rho)], Var f=integral_0^1 R(rho)d rho and R(rho)=sum_nonempty_S |S|rho^(|S|-1)fhat(S)^2 in the normalized centered product basis.
assumptions: Finite m, 0<p<1, 0<=rho<=1; replacement bits and retention choices independent across coordinates and independent of eta.
source: owner-own-work rederivation; standard special case of Ahlberg-Deijfen-Sfragara arXiv:2302.11367v2 Proposition 6
proof: Orthonormality and the coordinate coupling imply cross moments 1_{A=B}rho^|A|. Discrete gradient removes coordinate i with factor 1/sqrt(p(1-p)). Summing over i counts |S|, and integrating rho^(|S|-1) cancels this factor. ATTEMPT.md L2. Exact controls: MEASUREMENTS.json, 4 variance identities and 15 gradient correlations.
remaining_gap: No asymptotic rate of R is proved.

statement: For finite-graph passage time with weights a+Delta eta_e, Delta>0, deterministically chosen minimizers gamma_e^0 and gamma_e^1 after forcing e low/high satisfy Delta 1_{e in gamma_e^1}<=delta_e T<=Delta 1_{e in gamma_e^0}. With D=p(1-p)sum_e E(delta_e T)^2, q Delta^2 E H<=D<=p Delta^2 E L, where H,L count high/low edges on the unforced chosen minimizer.
assumptions: Finite connected graph, fixed endpoints, 0<a<b, Delta=b-a, iid Bernoulli(p), 0<p<1, q=1-p; one fixed deterministic tie order used in every environment.
source: owner-own-work elementary variational argument; ATTEMPT.md L3
proof: A low minimizer avoiding e remains a competitor of identical cost after raising e, forcing delta=0. A high minimizer containing e becomes cheaper by Delta after lowering e, forcing delta=Delta since delta<=Delta. Condition on eta_e: sums of forced membership probabilities equal EH/p and EL/q. Exact controls check 544 forcing cases and 4 energy sandwiches in MEASUREMENTS.json.
remaining_gap: Selected forced minimizers cannot automatically be replaced by an arbitrary unforced-overlap convention.

statement: In planar iid FPP with tau_e=1+eta_e and eta_e~Bernoulli(99/100), the finite-product resampling energy D_n=pq sum_e E[(delta_e T(0,n e1))^2] satisfies n/600<=D_n<=(99/50)n for every integer n>=1.
assumptions: Nearest-neighbor Z^2, endpoint n e1, weights 1 or 2, P(weight 1)=1/100; finite deterministic localization from C002; gradients squared inside expectation.
proof: For a simple length ell path, fewer than ell/4 high edges has probability <=2^ell q^(3ell/4). At most 4*3^(ell-1) paths start at 0. The union probability for ell>=n is <=(4/3)r^n/(1-r)<1/3 for r=6q^(3/4)=3/(5sqrt(10))<1/5. Every minimizer has length >=n, so EH>=n/6. C004 yields D_n>=q EH>=n/600. Its upper bound and length<=2n yield D_n<=2pn=(99/50)n.
remaining_gap: Linear resampling energy does not determine the integrated variance or chi.
novelty: No novelty claimed; independent audit required

statement: For the law in C005, define nu_n(S)=|S|That_n(S)^2/D_n over nonempty subsets of the localized edge set, K=|S|. Then Var T_n=D_n E_nu_n[1/K]. Thus Var T_n=n^(2/3+o(1)) is equivalent to E_nu_n[1/K]=n^(-1/3+o(1)).
assumptions: All assumptions of C005; normalized Bernoulli product Fourier coefficients; D_n>0 by C005.
source: owner-own-work reduction using C003 and C005; ATTEMPT.md L5
proof: The nu_n masses sum to 1 by the energy identity. Dividing each size-biased mass by |S| and summing recovers Parseval variance/D_n. Two-sided linear D_n bounds imply log D_n/log n->1. Exact controls check 4 harmonic identities; this does not verify the asymptotic estimate.
remaining_gap: G1: establish the harmonic spectral-mass estimate; both the estimate and KPZ conclusion remain unproved.

statement: G1: E_nu_n[1/K]=n^(-1/3+o(1)) for the size-biased passage-time spectral distribution of C006.
assumptions: The exact bounded planar iid law and spectral distribution in C005-C006.
source: owner-own-work proposed research obligation; ATTEMPT.md G1
proof: No proof. Qualitative noise chaos, a typical spectral scale, and logarithmic sublinear variance are insufficient by themselves.
remaining_gap: The single hardest remaining gap: quantitative control of the small-degree spectral tail.
novelty: Equivalent reformulation for this law, no novelty claim

statement: Convergence K_n/n^(1/3)->1 in probability does not imply E[1/K_n]=n^(-1/3+o(1)).
assumptions: Abstract integer-valued positive K_n; no assertion that the example is an FPP spectral distribution.
proof: Assign mass n^(-1/4) to K_n=1 and the rest to K_n=ceil(n^(1/3)). Then the scaled K_n converges in probability to 1, while E[1/K_n]>=n^(-1/4). At n=4096 the actual harmonic mean is 23/128 versus the naive 1/16; MEASUREMENTS.json rejects that shortcut.
remaining_gap: An FPP argument must rule out low-degree leakage rather than assume its absence.
